sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Greenhouse Effect**: The process by which **Greenhouse Gases (GHGs)** trap infrared radiation, warming the Earth's surface. Essential for life, but intensified by human activity.
• **Radiative Forcing**: The difference between incoming solar radiation and outgoing infrared radiation; positive values indicate warming.
• **Global Warming Potential (GWP)**: A measure of how much heat a gas traps in the atmosphere relative to **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** over a specific time horizon (usually 100 years).
• **Climate Sensitivity**: The equilibrium temperature change resulting from a doubling of atmospheric CO2 concentration.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Carbon Sequestration**: Capturing and storing atmospheric CO2 via biological (afforestation) or geological (CCS) means.
• **Climate Adaptation**: Adjusting systems to minimize damage from climate impacts (e.g., drought-resistant crops).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) conflict, climate finance gaps, and technological transfer barriers.
• **Solutions**: Decarbonization, circular economy, and nature-based solutions (NbS).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-M-N-F' (Major GHGs)
• **Decoded Meaning**: CO2 (Carbon Dioxide), Methane (CH4), Nitrous Oxide (N2O), Fluorinated Gases (HFCs, PFCs, SF6).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Climate Change' with 'Global Warming'. Global warming is the rise in average temperature; Climate Change includes warming AND its side effects (sea-level rise, extreme weather).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Anthropocene' to describe the current geological epoch where human activity is the dominant influence on climate.

keyTakeaways: Climate change is driven by the imbalance in the Earth's energy budget.
GHGs have varying GWP; CO2 is the baseline, but Methane has higher short-term warming potential.
Policy frameworks like the Paris Agreement rely on the principle of CBDR-RC.
